# :material-book-open-variant: Command reference { .dp-cli-title }

Every command and option of `depictio` 1.21.0, generated from its `--help`; `depictio <command> -h` prints the same. `depictio` alone prints a quick start, and `depictio-cli` is the same command. For step-by-step use, see [Common tasks](tasks.md). Scripts and AI agents can read the same reference as JSON: [`cli-reference.json`](cli-reference.json){ download }.

## :material-laptop: <span id="local-commands"></span>`local` { #local .dp-cli-group .dp-yellow }

Run a complete Depictio server on this machine, without Docker.
{ .dp-cli-lede }

:material-book-open-page-variant: [Python package](../installation/local.md)
{ .dp-cli-see }

### `local up` { #local-up .dp-cli-cmd .dp-yellow }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-yellow }
depictio local up [OPTIONS]
```

Start MongoDB, Redis, SeaweedFS, the API and the worker on this machine.

Run from a source checkout, it first builds the viewer when its sources changed since the last build (this needs pnpm).

Then add data with: `depictio ingest <results dir> --server local`

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="local-up-examples">--examples</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Example projects to seed on the first run: iris,penguins (the default), iris, penguins or none |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="local-up-port">--port</code> | <span class="dp-type">integer</span> |  | API/viewer port, kept for later runs (default: the previous one, else 8058 or a free one) |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="local-up-open">--open</code> <span class="dp-sep">/</span> <code class="dp-flag">--no-open</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> | on | Open the dashboards page in a browser |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="local-up-screenshots">--screenshots</code> <span class="dp-sep">/</span> <code class="dp-flag">--no-screenshots</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> | off | Dashboard thumbnails via Playwright; installs Chromium (~150 MB) if needed. Off by default. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="local-up-data-root-allow">--data-root-allow</code> | <span class="dp-type">path</span> <span class="dp-type dp-multi">repeatable</span> |  | Also let the web UI read run folders under PATH. Your home folder is always allowed. |

### `local open` { #local-open .dp-cli-cmd .dp-yellow }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-yellow }
depictio local open
```

Open the dashboards page of the running local server in a browser.

### `local down` { #local-down .dp-cli-cmd .dp-yellow }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-yellow }
depictio local down
```

Stop every process started by `depictio local up`.

### `local status` { #local-status .dp-cli-cmd .dp-yellow }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-yellow }
depictio local status
```

Show which local processes are running and whether the API answers.

Exits with 0 when every process runs and the API answers, 1 otherwise.

### `local wipe` { #local-wipe .dp-cli-cmd .dp-yellow }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-yellow }
depictio local wipe [OPTIONS]
```

Stop the server and delete all local data (downloaded binaries are kept).

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="local-wipe-yes">--yes</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Do not ask for confirmation |

### `local export` { #local-export .dp-cli-cmd .dp-yellow }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-yellow }
depictio local export [OPTIONS]
```

Also `depictio local export-compose`, its former name.
{ .dp-cli-also }

Copy the local server's data into a directory Docker Compose runs as is.

A running local server is stopped first, so the copy is consistent. Formerly `export-compose`.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="local-export-out">--out</code> | <span class="dp-type">path</span> | `depictio-docker` | Directory to create for the Docker Compose stack |

## :material-database-import: <span id="ingest-command"></span><span id="run-command"></span>`ingest` { #ingest .dp-cli-group .dp-purple }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-purple }
depictio ingest [OPTIONS] [DATA_DIR]
```

Also `depictio run`, its former name.
{ .dp-cli-also }

Ingest pipeline results into a Depictio server, from validation to dashboards. Formerly `run`.

Runs these steps in order:

1. Check that the server answers
2. Check the S3 storage configuration
3. Validate the project configuration (or resolve the template)
4. Sync the project configuration to the server
5. Scan the data files
6. Process the data collections, uploading images where local_images_path is set
7. Run the table joins the project configuration defines
8. Import the dashboards the project lacks (from the template, or from `--dashboard`)

Example, the template detected from the results directory:

```bash
depictio ingest results/
```

Refreshed after a new run, the dashboards kept as edited in the viewer:

```bash
depictio ingest results/ --update-config
```

A manifest-driven template, the files listed in a manifest instead of a directory:

```bash
depictio ingest --template generic/manifest-tables/1 --manifest https://data.example.org/run42/manifest.json
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-arg" id="ingest-data-dir">DATA_DIR</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Directory of the pipeline results to ingest, or an s3:// prefix holding them (e.g. `s3://my-bucket/pipeline/run42`). Without `--template` or `--project-config-path`, the template is detected from it. Formerly `--data-root`. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-server">--server</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | `local` for the one `depictio local up` runs, or a CLI configuration file. See [Which server a command uses](#choosing-a-server). |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-template">--template</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Template to build the project from, e.g. nf-core/ampliseq/2.16.0, or nf-core/ampliseq/latest for the newest shipped version. Default: detected from DATA_DIR, else composed from the catalog. Not with `--project-config-path`. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-project-config-path">--project-config-path</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Project YAML, for a pipeline Depictio ships no template for. Not with `--template`. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-update-config">--update-config</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Refresh a project that exists: its configuration, and its tables with every run rescanned. Its runs become those of DATA_DIR (or of the project file's locations) and those added with `--attach-run`; the runs of any other location are removed. Its dashboards are kept as they are, edits made in the viewer included; the template's dashboards it lacks are added. A project not on the server yet is created. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-var">--var</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> <span class="dp-type dp-multi">repeatable</span> |  | Extra template variable as KEY=VALUE. Repeatable. Example: `--var SAMPLESHEET_FILE=/path/to/samplesheet.csv` `--var METADATA_FILE=/path/to/metadata.tsv` |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-dry-run">--dry-run</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Validate the project configuration locally and list the steps that would run, without contacting the server |

**Project and runs**
{ .dp-cli-panel }

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-manifest">--manifest</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | A data manifest, as an https:// URL or a local file, listing the files to ingest as {id, type, url[, run]} entries. In place of DATA_DIR, for a manifest-driven template such as generic/manifest-tables/1 (it sets the template's MANIFEST_URL variable). |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-project">--project</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Project name. Replaces the name the template gives, or the `name` in the `--project-config-path` file. `--attach-run` and `--update-config` find the project by it. Formerly `--project-name`. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-attach-run">--attach-run</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Add DATA_DIR to an EXISTING project as one more run, instead of creating a project. The run is recorded as attached, so a later `--update-config` keeps it. The project is found by `--project`, else by the template's own name. Implies `--update-config`, dashboards included. Only the new run's rows are written; a recipe that mixes samples (distances, ordinations, top-N) is recomputed over every run, see `--per-run`. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-drop-missing-runs">--drop-missing-runs</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | On a refresh, remove the runs of a location added with `--attach-run` that is not on this host. Without it, such a refresh stops before changing anything. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-provenance-file">--provenance-file</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> <span class="dp-type dp-multi">repeatable</span> |  | Extra provenance/recap file (json, yaml, or 2-column tsv of key/value) whose entries are listed in the project's run-provenance report under 'User provided'. Repeatable. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-bind">--bind</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> <span class="dp-type dp-multi">repeatable</span> |  | Point one data collection at where its data actually is, as TAG=LOCATION. Repeatable. The scan mode is inferred from the location: a local directory or glob scans locally, a local file is a single file, https:// is a remote file, an s3:// prefix or glob is listed remotely. Example: `--bind` samples=`s3://my-bucket/run42/*.samples.csv` |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-compose">--compose</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Compose the template from what the catalog recognises in DATA_DIR, even when a bundled template fits. Without it, composing is the fallback when none does. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-include-unknown">--include-unknown</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | When composing: also ingest the tabular files the catalog does not recognise, in an 'Other data' tab. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-include">--include</code> | <span class="dp-type">glob</span> <span class="dp-type dp-multi">repeatable</span> |  | When composing: ingest the unrecognised files matching this glob, relative to DATA_DIR (e.g. `stats/*.tsv`). Repeatable. |

**Dashboards**
{ .dp-cli-panel }

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-dashboard">--dashboard</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> <span class="dp-type dp-multi">repeatable</span> |  | Dashboard YAML file to import instead of the template's own. Repeatable. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-dashboard-name">--dashboard-name</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Title of the main dashboard. Without it, a new dashboard takes the title in its YAML and a refresh keeps the current one, even if renamed in the viewer. With it, a refresh renames the existing main dashboard and leaves its contents as they are. Child tabs keep their titles and stay attached. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-reset-dashboards">--reset-dashboards</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Import the template's dashboards (or `--dashboard`'s) over the ones the project has: the layout and components edited in the viewer are lost, the titles are kept. Implies `--update-config`, as only a project that exists has dashboards to reset. |

**Scope and steps**
{ .dp-cli-panel }

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-workflow-name">--workflow-name</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Scan and process only this workflow (its tag) |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-data-collection-tag">--data-collection-tag</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Scan and process only this data collection |
| <span id="skipping-steps"></span><code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-skip">--skip</code> | <span class="dp-type">step</span> <span class="dp-type dp-multi">repeatable</span> |  | Steps to skip, comma-separated or repeated: server-check, s3-check, sync, scan, process, join, dashboards. Skipping process skips the image upload too. Formerly the `--skip-<step>` flags. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-continue-on-error">--continue-on-error</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Continue execution even if a step fails |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-sync-changed">--sync-changed</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Re-upload only the files whose size or modification time moved since the last scan. Narrower than `--update-config`, which re-uploads every file. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-write-mode">--write-mode</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> | `overwrite` | How step 6 writes a table. overwrite: rewrite it whole. replace-runs: partition it by run and rewrite only the runs in this batch, leaving the others untouched. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-incremental-write">--incremental-write</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | With `--write-mode` replace-runs, rewrite only the runs that changed instead of rebuilding the whole table. Falls back to a full rebuild whenever that cannot be done safely (run removed, table not partitioned by run, column type changed). |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-per-run">--per-run</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Compute every recipe once per run, including those that mix samples (distances, ordinations, top-N cuts), which are otherwise recomputed over all the project's runs at once. Their per-run outputs are then stacked. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-skip-unchanged">--skip-unchanged</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Leave a data collection's table untouched when the scan found no new, changed or removed file for it. Off by default, so that ingesting again always rebuilds a project that drifted. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-repartition">--repartition</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Let `--write-mode` replace-runs partition by run a table that is not yet. This rewrites every row, so it is never done implicitly, and never by the watcher. |

**Automation**
{ .dp-cli-panel }

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-pipeline-id">--pipeline-id</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | The pipeline that produced the data, as `<name>/<version>` (e.g. `nf-core/ampliseq/2.16.0`). Without `--template` or `--project-config-path`, the bundled template that matches it is used; otherwise it is ignored. Pipeline triggers fill it in, from a Nextflow pipeline's workflow.manifest for instance. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-triggered-by">--triggered-by</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> | `manual` | What invoked this ingestion, recorded on the project and shown in its ingestion report. Defaults to `manual`; a pipeline's completion trigger passes its engine (e.g. `nextflow`) so an automated project is distinguishable from one someone ingested by hand. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-user">--user</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Provision (create-or-get) this user's account and run the pipeline as them, then emit a passwordless login link to their dashboard. Requires `--provisioning-key`. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-provisioning-key">--provisioning-key</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Shared provisioning secret used with `--user` (or set DEPICTIO_AUTH_PROVISIONING_API_KEY). <span class="dp-env">env <code>DEPICTIO_AUTH_PROVISIONING_API_KEY</code></span> |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-result-json">--result-json</code> | <span class="dp-type">file</span> |  | Write how the ingestion ended (status, project and dashboard ids and links) to this file as JSON, for scripts. |

**Performance and debugging**
{ .dp-cli-panel }

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-streaming">--streaming</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Stream the Delta write instead of materialising the whole table in memory (lower peak RSS on large ingests). Experimental; falls back to the standard write on any failure. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-concurrency">--concurrency</code> | <span class="dp-type">integer</span> | `4` | Parallel HTTP requests for file uploads and cleanup deletes |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-upload-chunk-size">--upload-chunk-size</code> | <span class="dp-type">integer</span> | `1000` | Files per /files/upsert_batch request |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-state-cache">--state-cache</code> <span class="dp-sep">/</span> <code class="dp-flag">--no-state-cache</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> | on | Skip the runs whose file tree is unchanged since the last successful scan, from a local cache. Only applies when rescanning. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-async-upsert">--async-upsert</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Ask the server to profile each written table in the background, and poll until it finishes, instead of holding one long request open. A server without offloading enabled ignores it and answers inline. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-preview-recipes">--preview-recipes</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Show recipe input sources and transformed output before writing to Delta Lake |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="ingest-rich-tables">--rich-tables</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Show detailed summary of the workflow execution |

## :material-eye-refresh: <span id="watch-command"></span>`watch` { #watch .dp-cli-group .dp-violet }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-violet }
depictio watch [OPTIONS] [DATA_DIR]
```

Ingest pipeline results, then again whenever they change: `ingest` on a loop.

The first cycle runs at once and refreshes the project as `ingest --update-config` does; the later ones rescan and rewrite what moved. Runs until interrupted: SIGINT or SIGTERM finish the cycle in progress and then exit cleanly, so it is safe to run under systemd or as a container command.

One watcher or ingestion per project at a time: the first cycle takes the project's lock before it writes anything, and the watch holds it until it exits. A second one stops at once and names the lock file.

Example, rewriting only the runs that changed:

```bash
depictio watch results/ --write-mode replace-runs --incremental-write
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-arg" id="watch-data-dir">DATA_DIR</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Directory of the pipeline results to watch. Without `--template` or `--project-config-path`, the template is detected from it, as `ingest` does. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="watch-server">--server</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | `local` for the one `depictio local up` runs, or a CLI configuration file. See [Which server a command uses](#choosing-a-server). |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="watch-template">--template</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Template to build the project from, as for `ingest`. Default: detected from DATA_DIR. Not with `--project-config-path`. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="watch-project-config-path">--project-config-path</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Project YAML, for a pipeline Depictio ships no template for. Not with `--template`. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="watch-project">--project</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Project name. Replaces the name the template gives, or the `name` in the `--project-config-path` file. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="watch-var">--var</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> <span class="dp-type dp-multi">repeatable</span> |  | Extra template variable as KEY=VALUE. Repeatable. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="watch-mode">--mode</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> | `incremental` | incremental: re-upload only the files that changed. full: re-upload and rewrite everything on every cycle. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="watch-backend">--backend</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> | `auto` | auto (detect), native (filesystem events only), polling (periodic re-walk), or both. auto selects polling on network filesystems, where native events do not see writes made from another host. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="watch-debounce">--debounce</code> | <span class="dp-type">number</span> | `30` | Seconds of quiet before a cycle is triggered |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="watch-settle">--settle</code> | <span class="dp-type">number</span> | `5` | Seconds a file must hold the same size and mtime before it is ingested |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="watch-interval">--interval</code> | <span class="dp-type">number</span> | `300` | Seconds between polling walks (also the backstop for lost events) |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="watch-max-delay">--max-delay</code> | <span class="dp-type">number</span> | `300` | Ceiling on debouncing, so a tree written continuously still gets ingested |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="watch-full-every">--full-every</code> | <span class="dp-type">integer</span> |  | Run a full cycle every N incremental ones |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="watch-once">--once</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Run a single cycle and exit with its status |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="watch-max-runs">--max-runs</code> | <span class="dp-type">integer</span> |  | Stop after this many cycles, the first included |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="watch-write-mode">--write-mode</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> | `overwrite` | How each cycle writes a table, as for `ingest`: overwrite or replace-runs |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="watch-incremental-write">--incremental-write</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | With `--write-mode` replace-runs, rewrite only the runs that changed instead of rebuilding the whole table. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="watch-drop-missing-runs">--drop-missing-runs</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Remove the runs of a location added with `ingest --attach-run` that is not on this host. Without it, such a project stops the first cycle. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="watch-concurrency">--concurrency</code> | <span class="dp-type">integer</span> | `4` | Parallel HTTP requests during each cycle |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="watch-dry-run">--dry-run</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Report each cycle's changes without writing to the server |

### `config show` { #config-show .dp-cli-cmd .dp-green }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-green }
depictio config show [OPTIONS]
```

Show the current Depictio CLI configuration.

With `--project-name`, additionally fetch and print that project's metadata as registered on the server.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |

### `config nextflow` { #config-nextflow .dp-cli-cmd .dp-green }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-green }
depictio config nextflow [OPTIONS]
```

Print the path of the bundled Nextflow onComplete snippet.

Meant to be substituted straight into a Nextflow command, which is the whole reason it exists: the snippet lives inside the installed package, and that is not a path anyone should have to type or keep in sync.

```bash
nextflow run nf-core/ampliseq --outdir results -c $(depictio config nextflow)
```

For an nf-core pipeline that is the entire setup. The snippet reads the pipeline's own manifest and hands it to the CLI as `--pipeline-id`, which resolves the bundled template, so there is nothing else to configure.

Use `--print` to read the snippet, or to copy it somewhere you can edit:

```bash
depictio config nextflow --print > depictio.config
```

Use `--install` to stop repeating the `-c`, once per machine:

```bash
depictio config nextflow --install
```

Every later `nextflow run` then triggers Depictio with no extra flag, and `--uninstall` reverses it. Add `--default-disabled` to install it opt-in instead: pipelines then need `--depictio_enabled true` to trigger. Either way, `--depictio_enabled true/false` on a given `nextflow run` always wins.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="config-nextflow-print">--print</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Write the snippet's contents to stdout instead of its path. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="config-nextflow-install">--install</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Enable the trigger for every pipeline on this machine, once. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="config-nextflow-uninstall">--uninstall</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Undo `--install`, leaving any other Nextflow settings alone. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="config-nextflow-default-enabled">--default-enabled</code> <span class="dp-sep">/</span> <code class="dp-flag">--default-disabled</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> | on | With `--install`: whether a pipeline that sets no `--depictio_enabled` triggers Depictio (default) or stays opt-in. |

:material-book-open-page-variant: [Nextflow trigger](nextflow-trigger.md)
{ .dp-cli-see }


This command processes the top-level `joins` configuration in your project YAML, joining data collections on the client side and optionally persisting the results as Delta tables.

### `data push-images` { #data-push-images .dp-cli-cmd .dp-teal }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-teal }
depictio data push-images [OPTIONS] SOURCE_DIRECTORY S3_DESTINATION
```

Also `depictio images push`, its former name.
{ .dp-cli-also }

Upload a directory of images to S3 storage, for an image data collection. Formerly `images push`.

The directory structure is kept, relative to the source directory, and images already in storage are skipped unless `--overwrite`. Upload to the collection's s3_base_folder: its image_column paths are relative to it. `depictio ingest` does this itself for a collection that sets local_images_path.

Examples:

```bash
# Push all images to S3
depictio data push-images ./data/images s3://my-bucket/project/images/

# Dry run to see what would be uploaded
depictio data push-images ./data/images s3://my-bucket/images/ --dry-run

# Push only specific extensions
depictio data push-images ./data/images s3://my-bucket/images/ --extensions ".png,.jpg"
```

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-arg" id="data-push-images-source-directory">SOURCE_DIRECTORY</code><br><span class="dp-badge dp-req">required</span> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Source directory containing images |
| <code class="dp-arg" id="data-push-images-s3-destination">S3_DESTINATION</code><br><span class="dp-badge dp-req">required</span> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | S3 destination path (e.g., `s3://bucket/path/to/images/`) |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="data-push-images-recursive">--recursive</code> <code class="dp-flag dp-short">-r</code> <span class="dp-sep">/</span> <code class="dp-flag">--no-recursive</code> <code class="dp-flag dp-short">-R</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> | on | Include subdirectories |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="data-push-images-extensions">--extensions</code> <code class="dp-flag dp-short">-e</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Comma-separated list of extensions to upload (e.g., `.png,.jpg`) |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="data-push-images-dry-run">--dry-run</code> <code class="dp-flag dp-short">-n</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Show what would be uploaded without actually uploading |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="data-push-images-overwrite">--overwrite</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Overwrite existing files in S3 |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="data-push-images-concurrency">--concurrency</code> <code class="dp-flag dp-short">-c</code> | <span class="dp-type">integer</span> | `8` | Number of parallel uploads |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="data-push-images-server">--server</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | `local` for the one `depictio local up` runs, or a CLI configuration file. See [Which server a command uses](#choosing-a-server). |

### `data vacuum` { #data-vacuum .dp-cli-cmd .dp-teal }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-teal }
depictio data vacuum [OPTIONS] DATA_COLLECTION_TAG
```

Remove Delta files no longer referenced by any retained version.

Nothing in depictio has ever vacuumed, so every re-ingestion has left its predecessor's files behind and a data collection's physical footprint grows without bound. A watcher accelerates that considerably.

Deliberately dry-run by default and never wired into an ingestion path: vacuuming below the retention window pulls files out from under an API worker that is part-way through reading the table.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-arg" id="data-vacuum-data-collection-tag">DATA_COLLECTION_TAG</code><br><span class="dp-badge dp-req">required</span> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Data collection whose stale Delta files to remove |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="data-vacuum-server">--server</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | `local` for the one `depictio local up` runs, or a CLI configuration file. See [Which server a command uses](#choosing-a-server). |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="data-vacuum-project-config-path">--project-config-path</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Project configuration file (YAML) |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="data-vacuum-retention-hours">--retention-hours</code> | <span class="dp-type">integer</span> | `168` | Keep files needed by versions newer than this. Going below the 168h default breaks readers that are mid-query. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="data-vacuum-apply">--apply</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Actually delete. Without this the command only reports. |

:material-book-open-page-variant: [Data versions](../features/versioning.md#data-versions)
{ .dp-cli-see }

## :material-view-dashboard-edit: <span id="dashboard-commands"></span>`dashboard` { #dashboard .dp-cli-group .dp-blue }

Validate, import and export dashboard YAML files.
{ .dp-cli-lede }

:material-book-open-page-variant: [Dashboard YAML](../features/yaml-sync.md)
{ .dp-cli-see }

### `dashboard validate` { #dashboard-validate .dp-cli-cmd .dp-blue }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-blue }
depictio dashboard validate [OPTIONS] YAML_FILE
```

Validate a dashboard YAML file.

Runs two levels of validation:

1. Schema + domain (always): required fields, enum values, cross-field rules (visu_type, mode/code_content, aggregation×column_type, etc.)

2. Server schema (when a server is configured): resolves each component's workflow_tag + data_collection_tag against the server delta table schema, checks that column_name exists, and validates aggregation/interactive_component_type against the inferred column type. Without `--server` it uses the default server (`$DEPICTIO_CLI_CONFIG_PATH`, else `~/.depictio/CLI.yaml`, else the local server), is skipped when that has no configuration, and what it reports is shown as warnings only. Use `--offline` to skip it.

Example:

```bash
depictio dashboard validate dashboard.yaml --server local
depictio dashboard validate dashboard.yaml --server admin_config.yaml --offline
depictio dashboard validate dashboard.yaml  # offline unless a default server is set up
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-arg" id="dashboard-validate-yaml-file">YAML_FILE</code><br><span class="dp-badge dp-req">required</span> | <span class="dp-type">path</span> |  | Path to YAML dashboard file |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="dashboard-validate-server">--server</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | `local` for the one `depictio local up` runs, or a CLI configuration file. See [Which server a command uses](#choosing-a-server). |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="dashboard-validate-verbose">--verbose</code> <code class="dp-flag dp-short">-v</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | No effect, kept for the scripts that pass it. For detailed logs, put `-v` before the command: depictio `-v` dashboard validate ... |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="dashboard-validate-offline">--offline</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Skip server schema validation (column names, inferred types, aggregation compatibility) |

### `dashboard import` { #dashboard-import .dp-cli-cmd .dp-blue }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-blue }
depictio dashboard import [OPTIONS] YAML_FILE
```

Import a dashboard YAML file to the server.

The project is determined in this order:

1. `--project` option (if provided)
2. project_tag field in the YAML file

Imports into the server `--server` names, else the one `$DEPICTIO_CLI_CONFIG_PATH` or `~/.depictio/CLI.yaml` describes, else the local server (none needed for `--dry-run` validation).

Example:

```bash
# Validate without a server
depictio dashboard import dashboard.yaml --dry-run

# Import into the server `depictio local up` runs
depictio dashboard import dashboard.yaml --server local

# Overwrite existing dashboard with same title
depictio dashboard import dashboard.yaml --server admin_config.yaml --overwrite

# Override with explicit project ID
depictio dashboard import dashboard.yaml --server admin_config.yaml --project 646b0f3c1e4a2d7f8e5b8c9a

# Skip online column validation
depictio dashboard import dashboard.yaml --server admin_config.yaml --offline
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-arg" id="dashboard-import-yaml-file">YAML_FILE</code><br><span class="dp-badge dp-req">required</span> | <span class="dp-type">path</span> |  | Path to YAML dashboard file |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="dashboard-import-server">--server</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | `local` for the one `depictio local up` runs, or a CLI configuration file. See [Which server a command uses](#choosing-a-server). |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="dashboard-import-project">--project</code> <code class="dp-flag dp-short">-p</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Project ID (overrides project_tag in YAML) |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="dashboard-import-overwrite">--overwrite</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Overwrite existing dashboard with same title in project |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="dashboard-import-dry-run">--dry-run</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Validate only, don't import |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="dashboard-import-offline">--offline</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Skip online checks (column name validation against server DC schema) |

### `dashboard export` { #dashboard-export .dp-cli-cmd .dp-blue }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-blue }
depictio dashboard export [OPTIONS] DASHBOARD_ID
```

Export a dashboard from the server to a YAML file.

Downloads the dashboard configuration and saves it as a minimal YAML file suitable for version control and re-import.

Example:

```bash
depictio dashboard export 6824cb3b89d2b72169309737 --server local
depictio dashboard export 6824cb3b89d2b72169309737 --server admin_config.yaml -o my-dashboard.yaml
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-arg" id="dashboard-export-dashboard-id">DASHBOARD_ID</code><br><span class="dp-badge dp-req">required</span> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Dashboard ID to export |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="dashboard-export-server">--server</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | `local` for the one `depictio local up` runs, or a CLI configuration file. See [Which server a command uses](#choosing-a-server). |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="dashboard-export-output">--output</code> <code class="dp-flag dp-short">-o</code> | <span class="dp-type">path</span> | `dashboard.yaml` | Output file path |

## :material-layers-outline: <span id="template-commands"></span>`template` { #template .dp-cli-group .dp-orange }

Export a project and its dashboards as a template someone else can run on their data, or compose one from what the catalog recognises in a results directory.
{ .dp-cli-lede }

:material-book-open-page-variant: [Templates](../usage/projects/templates.md)
{ .dp-cli-see }

### `template export` { #template-export .dp-cli-cmd .dp-orange }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-orange }
depictio template export --template-id TEMPLATE_ID [OPTIONS] PROJECT_ID
```

Export a project + its dashboards as a template bundle.

The inverse of `depictio ingest --template`: the bundle can be ingested on another dataset.

Example:

```bash
depictio template export 6824cb3b89d2b72169309737 \
  --template-id my-lab/rnaseq-qc/1 --server admin_config.yaml -o depictio/projects
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-arg" id="template-export-project-id">PROJECT_ID</code><br><span class="dp-badge dp-req">required</span> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Project ID to export |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="template-export-template-id">--template-id</code> <code class="dp-flag dp-short">-t</code><br><span class="dp-badge dp-req">required</span> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Template id, e.g. `my-lab/rnaseq-qc/1` |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="template-export-server">--server</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | `local` for the one `depictio local up` runs, or a CLI configuration file. See [Which server a command uses](#choosing-a-server). |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="template-export-output-dir">--output-dir</code> <code class="dp-flag dp-short">-o</code> | <span class="dp-type">path</span> | `.` | Directory to unpack the bundle into |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="template-export-version">--version</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> | `1.0.0` | Template version |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="template-export-description">--description</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Template description |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="template-export-data-dir">--data-dir</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Local path prefix to re-parameterize as `{DATA_ROOT}` in the template |

:material-book-open-page-variant: [Export a project as a template](../usage/projects/templates.md#export-a-project-as-a-template)
{ .dp-cli-see }

### `template compose` { #template-compose .dp-cli-cmd .dp-orange }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-orange }
depictio template compose [OPTIONS] DATA_ROOT
```

Compose a template from the files the catalog recognises in a results directory.

Offline: nothing is ingested. Prints what was recognised, the tabs and key metrics of the dashboard, what was left out and why, and the tabular files nothing recognised with what each could show. This is what `depictio ingest <dir>` does by itself when no bundled template fits the run.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-arg" id="template-compose-data-root">DATA_ROOT</code><br><span class="dp-badge dp-req">required</span> | <span class="dp-type">path</span> |  | Results directory to compose a dashboard for |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="template-compose-output">--output</code> <code class="dp-flag dp-short">-o</code> | <span class="dp-type">path</span> |  | Write the template here, to edit it and ingest with it: `depictio ingest <dir> --template <out>`. Default: where `depictio ingest` keeps composed templates |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="template-compose-include-unknown">--include-unknown</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Also include the tabular files the catalog does not recognise |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="template-compose-include">--include</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> <span class="dp-type dp-multi">repeatable</span> |  | Include the unrecognised files matching this glob (relative to the directory); repeatable |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="template-compose-project">--project</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Name of the project to create |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="template-compose-verbose">--verbose</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | List everything left out, with the reason |

:material-book-open-page-variant: [Composed dashboards](../usage/projects/composed-dashboards.md#template-compose)
{ .dp-cli-see }

## :material-swap-horizontal-bold: <span id="migrate-commands"></span>`migrate` { #migrate .dp-cli-group .dp-red }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-red }
depictio migrate --project PROJECT [OPTIONS]
```

Migrate a project from one Depictio instance to another (non-destructive).

The project is read from `--server` and written to `--to-server`. DEPICTIO_CLI_TOKEN and DEPICTIO_CLI_API_BASE_URL apply to `--server` only.

Mode descriptions:

- `all`: MongoDB docs + S3 files (default, full first-time migration)
- `metadata`: MongoDB docs only (both instances share S3 storage)
- `dashboard`: Dashboards only (project already exists on remote)
- `files`: S3 files only (metadata already migrated)

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="migrate-project">--project</code><br><span class="dp-badge dp-req">required</span> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Project name to migrate |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="migrate-server">--server</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Server to migrate from. Server to use: `local` for the one `depictio local up` runs, or a CLI configuration file. Default: `$DEPICTIO_CLI_CONFIG_PATH`, else `~/.depictio/CLI.yaml`, else the local server. Formerly `--CLI-config-path`. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="migrate-to-server">--to-server</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Server to migrate to, given the same way as `--server`. Default: `~/.depictio/CLI_remote.yaml`. Formerly `--target-config`. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="migrate-mode">--mode</code> | <span class="dp-choices"><code class="dp-choice">all</code> <code class="dp-choice">metadata</code> <code class="dp-choice">dashboard</code> <code class="dp-choice">files</code></span> | `all` | Migration scope, described below. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="migrate-dry-run">--dry-run</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Preview changes without writing anything |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="migrate-overwrite">--overwrite</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Replace the project on the target if it already exists |

:material-book-open-page-variant: [Project migration](../usage/administration/migrate.md)
{ .dp-cli-see }

## :material-backup-restore: <span id="backup-commands"></span>`backup` { #backup .dp-cli-group .dp-red }

Create, list, validate and restore server database backups (admins only).
{ .dp-cli-lede }

:material-book-open-page-variant: [Backup and restore](../usage/administration/backup.md)
{ .dp-cli-see }

### `backup create` { #backup-create .dp-cli-cmd .dp-red }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-red }
depictio backup create [OPTIONS]
```

Create a backup of the Depictio database.

This command creates a full backup of the MongoDB database, excluding:

- Short-lived tokens
- Temporary users and their related resources

Optionally includes S3 deltatable data for complete backups.

Only administrators can perform backup operations.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="backup-create-server">--server</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | `local` for the one `depictio local up` runs, or a CLI configuration file. See [Which server a command uses](#choosing-a-server). |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="backup-create-dry-run">--dry-run</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Perform validation without creating backup |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="backup-create-include-s3-data">--include-s3-data</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Include S3 deltatable data in backup |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="backup-create-s3-backup-prefix">--s3-backup-prefix</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> | `backup` | Prefix for S3 backup location |

### `backup list` { #backup-list .dp-cli-cmd .dp-red }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-red }
depictio backup list [OPTIONS]
```

List available backup files on the server.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="backup-list-server">--server</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | `local` for the one `depictio local up` runs, or a CLI configuration file. See [Which server a command uses](#choosing-a-server). |

### `backup validate` { #backup-validate .dp-cli-cmd .dp-red }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-red }
depictio backup validate [OPTIONS] BACKUP_ID
```

Validate a backup file on the server against Pydantic models.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-arg" id="backup-validate-backup-id">BACKUP_ID</code><br><span class="dp-badge dp-req">required</span> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | ID of the backup to validate (format: YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS) |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="backup-validate-server">--server</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | `local` for the one `depictio local up` runs, or a CLI configuration file. See [Which server a command uses](#choosing-a-server). |

### `backup restore` { #backup-restore .dp-cli-cmd .dp-red }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-red }
depictio backup restore [OPTIONS] BACKUP_ID
```

Restore data from a backup file.

!!! warning

    This is a destructive operation that will replace existing data! Use `--dry-run` to preview what would be restored without making changes.

Before restoring, the server validates the backup against the current Pydantic models and refuses to restore invalid backups unless `--skip-validation` is passed.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-arg" id="backup-restore-backup-id">BACKUP_ID</code><br><span class="dp-badge dp-req">required</span> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | ID of the backup to restore (format: YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS) |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="backup-restore-server">--server</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | `local` for the one `depictio local up` runs, or a CLI configuration file. See [Which server a command uses](#choosing-a-server). |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="backup-restore-dry-run">--dry-run</code> <span class="dp-sep">/</span> <code class="dp-flag">--no-dry-run</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> | off | Simulate restore without making changes |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="backup-restore-collections">--collections</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Comma-separated list of collections to restore |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="backup-restore-force">--force</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Skip confirmation prompt (use with caution!) |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="backup-restore-allow-unverified">--allow-unverified</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Allow restoring a legacy backup without a checksum sidecar. Checksum mismatches are never bypassable. |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="backup-restore-skip-validation">--skip-validation</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Skip the server-side Pydantic validation gate before restore (dangerous!) |

## :material-bookshelf: <span id="catalog-commands"></span>`catalog` { #catalog .dp-cli-group .dp-blue }

Browse the supported tools and the dashboard components their outputs become.
{ .dp-cli-lede }

:material-book-open-page-variant: [Tools catalog](../catalog/index.md)
{ .dp-cli-see }

### `catalog list` { #catalog-list .dp-cli-cmd .dp-blue }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-blue }

```

List every tool + output with its recipe and render targets.

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-blue }

```

### `catalog preview` { #catalog-preview .dp-cli-cmd .dp-blue }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-blue }
depictio catalog preview [OPTIONS] OUTPUT_ID
```

Preview an output's components in the browser, on its bundled fixture.

Served on an ephemeral localhost server (Ctrl-C to stop); `--out FILE` exports a portable, self-contained HTML instead.

Renders every renders_as target through the depictio React viewer's real ComponentRenderer (figure/card/table today). The data is computed Dash-free from the output's bundled fixture. Needs the prebuilt bundle (cd depictio/viewer && pnpm run build:catalog-preview).

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-arg" id="catalog-preview-output-id">OUTPUT_ID</code><br><span class="dp-badge dp-req">required</span> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Output id, e.g. qiime2_alpha_diversity |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="catalog-preview-theme">--theme</code> <code class="dp-flag dp-short">-t</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> | `light` | Theme: light or dark |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="catalog-preview-out">--out</code> <code class="dp-flag dp-short">-o</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Export the self-contained HTML here instead of serving it |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="catalog-preview-port">--port</code> | <span class="dp-type">integer</span> | `0` | Port for the ephemeral server (0 = auto) |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="catalog-preview-no-open">--no-open</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Do not open a browser tab |

### `catalog gallery` { #catalog-gallery .dp-cli-cmd .dp-blue }

``` { .text .dp-cli-sig .dp-blue }
depictio catalog gallery [OPTIONS]
```

Browse the whole catalog on one page in the browser.

Every tool's outputs, grouped, with component-type badges, fixture chips, search/filter and copyable renders_as, served on an ephemeral localhost server (Ctrl-C to stop).

Clicking an output opens its full live preview (same renderer as catalog preview). Pass `--out FILE` to export a portable, self-contained HTML instead.

Served or exported, the page needs the prebuilt bundle (cd depictio/viewer && pnpm run build:catalog-preview).

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="catalog-gallery-theme">--theme</code> <code class="dp-flag dp-short">-t</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> | `light` | Theme: light or dark |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="catalog-gallery-out">--out</code> <code class="dp-flag dp-short">-o</code> | <span class="dp-type">text</span> |  | Export the self-contained HTML here instead of serving it |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="catalog-gallery-port">--port</code> | <span class="dp-type">integer</span> | `0` | Port for the ephemeral server (0 = auto) |
| <code class="dp-flag" id="catalog-gallery-no-open">--no-open</code> | <span class="dp-type">flag</span> |  | Do not open a browser tab |

    | `--var` | `ingest --server local` | `local up` |
    | `--verbose-level, -vl` | `--log-level` | `depictio` |
    | `images push` | `data push-images` |  |
    | `local export-compose` | `local export` |  |
    | `run` | `ingest` |  |

??? note "Maintainer commands, out of `--help`"

    For catalog authoring, recipe tests and CI. They may change without notice.

    | Command | Does |
    | --- | --- |
    | `depictio images list-bucket` | List images in an S3 bucket/prefix. |
    | `depictio dev recipe run` | Run a recipe against local data with all 5 validation checkpoints. |
    | `depictio dev recipe list` | List all available shared recipes. |
    | `depictio dev recipe info` | Show recipe details: docstring, sources, and output schema. |
    | `depictio dev catalog columns` | Print the output columns a recipe produces (to help write `roles`). |
    | `depictio dev catalog validate` | Validate the catalog (CI-friendly: non-zero on error). |
    | `depictio dev catalog match` | Recognise which catalog outputs are present in a run directory. |
    | `depictio dev catalog compose` | Preview the guided dashboard a run would compose (module → viz). |
    | `depictio dev catalog refresh-index` | Regenerate the vendored existence indices from authoritative sources. |
    | `depictio dev catalog schema` | Emit the JSON Schema for a catalog file (regenerate the committed copy). |
    | `depictio dev catalog kinds` | Emit the advanced_viz kind descriptors (source for tool-studio's kinds.json). |
    | `depictio dev catalog manifest` | Emit a JSON snapshot of the existing catalog (source for tool-studio's catalog.json). |
    | `depictio dev catalog figure-params` | Emit the figure builder's visualization list + per-viz parameter specs. |
    | `depictio dev backup check-coverage` | Check validation coverage for all MongoDB collections. |
    | `depictio dev link list` | List all DC links for a project. |
    | `depictio dev link create` | Create a new DC link for cross-DC filtering. |
    | `depictio dev link resolve` | Test link resolution by resolving filter values from source to target DC. |
    | `depictio dev link delete` | Delete a DC link. |
